alternative_explanations: The gain may come entirely from being handed the active source and random-access grid, making the event queue an ordinary BFS index rather than a learned cellular principle.
A monotone linearly separable rule may make scheduling trivial; richer learned dynamics could require revisiting dormant cells or global synchronization.
Operation counting may favor event execution even if irregular memory access is slower on hardware.
confounds: The local rule is learned from its complete four-case truth table, the corridor is synthetic and visible, and no raw perception or language interface is included.
K changes dense dormant area but not the size of the active causal corridor; this intentionally tests irrelevant-state scaling only.
falsification_criteria: Kill the current event-queue implementation if it is inexact, fails either single-damage or double-block cases, has query-operation K slope above 0.25, grows mean cell updates by more than 25% from K=8 to K=32 at fixed depth, or fails to save at least 50% query operations versus the matched synchronous learner at K=32 and D=4/6.

outcome_policy.negative: The event implementation loses correctness, damage behavior, or irrelevant-state scaling after full accounting; discard this implementation and reduce confidence in HYP-0006 without patching the benchmark.
outcome_policy.null: Event scheduling avoids the sweep but is cost-equivalent to or dominated by sparse BFS and supplies no distinct learned-cellular property; reduce HYP-0006 priority and test a different principle.
outcome_policy.positive: Sparse event scheduling preserves exact learned local propagation with near-zero irrelevant-state compute slope; retain only this bounded structural signature and use the BFS/oracle bounds to decide whether HYP-0006 merits an adversarial screen.

predicted_outcome: All non-random candidates reach accuracy, single-damage accuracy, and double-block accuracy 1.0. Learned synchronous compute has K slope between 1.5 and 2.3, while learned event-queue K slope is at most 0.15 and its mean cell updates at K=32 differ by at most 10% from K=8 at each depth. At K=32 and D=4/6, learned event query operations are at least 80% below the learned synchronous sweep. The oracle event queue and sparse BFS expose whether learned rule evaluation or generic graph traversal accounts for the remaining cost.
promotion_criteria: Quick budget cannot promote HYP-0006. A later screen is justified only if exactness and the preregistered K-scaling signature hold, learning and dense input-state costs are fully charged, and event dynamics show a robustness or transfer property not already matched more cheaply by sparse BFS.
research_question: With the same learned local transition rule and dense substrate representation, can event scheduling keep active computation independent of dormant grid size while preserving propagation and single-cell damage tolerance, or is the mechanism only sparse graph traversal?
title: Learned local rule: synchronous sweep versus event queue
